paragraphs.text: He prophecies that all nations will come to the knowledge of God, who then was only known in Judea.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: As the faithful obey God willingly, so the infidels disguise themselves as obedient out of fear.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: He refers to the slothful dullness of man, who is cold in the consideration of God's works.

paragraphs.text: His providence is wonderful in maintaining their estate.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: He proves that God will extend his grace also to the Gentiles, because he punishes among them such as will not obey his calling.
paragraphs.label: e

paragraphs.text: He signifies some special benefit that God had showed to his Church of the Jews, in delivering them from some great danger: of which he promises that the Gentiles will also be partakers.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: The condition of the Church is here described, which is to be led by God's providence into troubles, to be subject under tyrants, and to enter into many dangers.
paragraphs.label: g

paragraphs.text: The duty of the faithful is here described, who are never mindful to render God praise for his benefits.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: It is not enough to have received God's benefits and to be mindful of it, but also we are bound to make others profit by it and praise God.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: If I delight in wickedness, God will not hear me, but if I confess it, he will receive me.
